patch.value: Reconcile duplicate ownership of GitHub issue #5 blocking the gated tracker sync

Tracks gh:unbraind/pm-rlm#49 (filed 2026-11-01, missed by the blind issue watch). The scheduled gated sync still fails the ownership preflight ('GitHub issue #5 has multiple existing owners') on current main: two closed records both claim the source issue — the imported issue item holds the gh: tag/github_url, and the other closed record (pm-rlm-sr0b) begins its description with the source issue URL, which the identity contract treats as a competing ownership declaration. Latest failing run 41297675184 (2026-11-01T10:29Z, pm-github 2026.10.29); the 10-31 run passed, the 11-01 run after the sync-workflow bump refuses again. Reconcile exactly one import owner with supported PM operations while preserving both records' knowledge, evidence and durable history (reword the competing description or convert it to a structured relationship); keep the fail-closed guard.

value.text: Duplicate #4 and #5 ownership reconciled. Both competing records no longer lead their descriptions with 'GitHub issue <url>' (the source references are preserved in prose), each gained a related dependency to its imported record, and both stay closed. The imported records keep the gh: tags and github_url as sole owners. Measurement — before: failing run https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/actions/runs/41297675184 (2026-11-01T10:29Z, 'GitHub issue #5 has multiple existing owners'; #4 had the same competing shape). After: the same gated dry-run the scheduled workflow runs (pm-github 2026.10.29 as pinned by the reusable workflow) passes against this branch's tracker: fetched 6, planned 6, import 0, update 6, skip 0, provenance-indexed 10, and issues #4 and #5 resolve uniquely to their imported records via provenance-tag. The command is linked as a passing test; its pm-test receipt runs in pm's isolated seeded workspace, so the reconciliation numbers here come from the direct dry-run against this checkout. GitHub API budget was checked before measuring (core remaining above the 1500 floor). Guard unchanged; item stays open for orchestrator close after merge.

patch.value: Duplicate GitHub #4 and #5 ownership removed on this branch (pm-rlm-k7tv and pm-rlm-sr0b no longer lead with the issue URLs and link their imported records as related). Before: scheduled sync run 41297675184 refused with multiple existing owners. After: the same gated dry-run (pm-github 2026.10.29) passes against this tracker with import 0, update 6, skip 0. The merged result is re-checked by dispatching the scheduled sync after merge.

## Observed failure
The scheduled GitHub issue sync on current main `0bb9d6ed9956886de5df2f987b5f5640e38ea518`, using `pm-github@2026.10.29`, exits 1 at the ownership preflight:

> GitHub issue #5 has multiple existing owners; import plan is not idempotent. No item was written for this issue. No branch was published.

[Hosted run and failing job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/actions/runs/41297675184/job/124821865302). This is a repository tracker-data collision, not a demonstrated RLM inference/runtime defect. The fail-closed guard is working and should remain.

## Exact competing records
Both records are closed, but both declare ownership of [issue #5](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/issues/5):
- [pm-rlm-sr0b](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/blob/0bb9d6ed9956886de5df2f987b5f5640e38ea518/.agents/pm/issues/pm-rlm-sr0b.toon): description begins `GitHub issue https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/issues/5.`; this is an ownership declaration, not an incidental prose mention. It retains implementation evidence and regression references.
- [pm-rlm-github-dfe63798395a-5](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/blob/0bb9d6ed9956886de5df2f987b5f5640e38ea518/.agents/pm/issues/pm-rlm-github-dfe63798395a-5.toon): exact `gh:unbraind/pm-rlm#5` tag plus `github_url`, `github_number: 5` and imported provider metadata.

The pinned [identity contract](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-github/blob/da0366ac6e81f35ce66bcfe5efb3b386a1c3fd84/docs/identity-collisions.md) explicitly recognizes leading declarations and structured provenance as claims. Its narrow tag-only repair is not suitable for two independently declared owners; manually reviewed ownership reconciliation is required.

## Expected outcome and impact
One unambiguous import owner for each GitHub identity, while both historical records, their content, delivery evidence, relationships and append-only histories remain recoverable. The current collision blocks the scheduled tracker refresh; no data loss or published-branch mutation is established by this observation.

## Reproduction / limits
Inspect the two records on the immutable commit above and the referenced hosted sync log. A read-only identity diagnosis can further show their claims. No local provider import, repair mutation, model call or full RLM suite was executed in this review. The workflow-version-only merge exposed this failure, but this report does not claim it created the older duplicate records.

## Acceptance / regression criteria
- Independently select the canonical provider owner and represent the other record as a durable related implementation record without a second ownership declaration. Do not delete either record or its history to silence the guard.
- Back up and verify recoverability before the audited repair; preserve original IDs, content, relationships, completion/release provenance and existing history bytes.
- Diagnose the complete all-status tracker, including any further collisions, rather than fixing only the first reported identity.
- Verify one import owner for #5, an initial complete sync and a repeated idempotent sync, with no unrelated item changes and no new duplicates.
- Retain fail-closed ambiguity, scoped commit and privacy gates, and record exact revision/commands/results.

## Dedup
Checked all 48 existing all-status issues/PRs, their available conversation comments and all 36 current canonical PM records. #5 is the delivered runtime validation fix, not this sync ownership repair. No dedicated existing repair owner was found.
